وزیر نے ضمانت دی کہ بینظیر بھٹو کے قتل کے لیے مسؤول افراد کے خلاف ضرور عمل ہوگا۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ جو بھی ذمہدار پاتا چلا وہ اس کے خلاف عمل کرے گا۔

جو افسران او ایس ڈی بنایے گئے ہیں ان میں راولپنڈی کے صدیق سٹی پولیس افسر سعود عزیز، صدیق ڈسٹریکٹ کوارڈینٹر افسر عرفان الہی، اضافی انسپکٹر جنرل پولیس راولپنڈی چوہدری عبدالمجید، سپرنٹنڈنٹ پولیس اشفاق انور، سپرنٹنڈنٹ پولیس آپریشنز یاسین فاروق، ایس پی خرم شہزاد اور ڈائرکٹر جنرل آف سول ڈیفنس ریتائرد جاوید اقبال چیمہ شامل ہیں۔ ان کا کنٹریکٹ منسوخ کر دیا گیا ہے۔

اسلام آباد سے ہمارے خبرنگار ذوالفقار علی کے مطابق، ابھی تک افسران کو او ایس ڈی بنانے کا رسمی نوٹیفیکیشن جاری نہیں ہوا ہے۔

یاد رکھیں کہ ایم ایس نے پاکستانی حکومت کو بینظیر بھٹو کے قتل کے ذمہداران کو کیفر کردار تک پہنچانے کا تکلیف دیا تھا۔ ایم ایس کی رپورٹ میں بینظیر بھٹو کی سیکیورٹی پر مامور پیپلز پارٹی کے کچھ عہدیداروں کا بھی ذکر ہے جن کا کوئی فیصلہ ابھی نہیں ہوا ہے۔

The Federal Information and Broadcasting Minister, Qamar Zaman Kaira, informed the BBC that the officers referenced in the United Nations report have been assigned as Officers on Special Duty (OSDs). Their names have additionally been added to the Exit Control List (ECL).

Minister Kaira assured that definitive action will be taken against those held accountable for the assassination of Benazir Bhutto. He emphasized that anyone found culpable will face consequences.

Notably, among those designated as OSDs are former Rawalpindi City Police Officer Saud Aziz, former District Coordinator Officer Iftikhar Ali, Additional Inspector General of Police Rawalpindi Chaudhry Abdul Majeed, Superintendent of Police Ashfaq Anwar, Superintendent of Police Operations Yasin Farooq, SP Khurram Shehzad, and Retired Director-General of Soldier Defense Javed Iqbal Cheema. Their contracts have been terminated.

Our correspondent from Islamabad, Zulfiqar Ali, reports that an official notification to appoint these officers as OSDs has not been issued as of yet.

It is pertinent to recall that the UN had mandated the Pakistani government to bring Benazir Bhutto's assassins to justice. The UN report also names certain People's Party officials who were responsible for her security and currently hold high-ranking positions; however, no decisions have been made concerning them.

'A mere handful remain from the generation that witnessed the genocide of 1947. Yet, from North India to Attock, if you ask any elderly person about the killers today, they'll say, 'We weren't the killers; they came from outside.'

But who were the victims? They were all from our own neighborhoods. Did anyone save anyone? Yes, I saved Karam Chand, and I saved Mohammed Aslam's family. Would we recognize the killers if they stood before us today?

No, they say, 'It was an attack.' But attacks are faceless. Do the victims remember? Yes, there was Shyam, Sardar Mohammed, Partap Singh, Kareem's wife and daughter, and Krishna's brother.

From 1947 until now, in every corner of Delhi, you'll still hear the same story from every community - Shia, Sunni, Hindu, Muslim, migrant, Sindhi, Bengali, Bahari, Dalit Brahmin, and others. 'We didn't kill; they came from outside.' I saved someone, and someone saved me.

When any group, religious or otherwise, remains oppressed, they internalize each individual's pain as their own. Once freed, their mindset, behavior, and consciousness, whether consciously or unconsciously, remain shaped by their oppressors' presence.

Recall the British Raj police perceived as so brutal? The moment we gained independence, we started defending those very police stations. Until yesterday, when the British declared a state of emergency, we deemed it tyranny. Today, when anyone demands freedom, we brand them as enemies of the state and label their actions as terrorism.
We've mastered something the British couldn't—how to transform an entire region into a prison, choking it with tear gas or drowning it in black water. And for the people, we administer a dose of madness.

Certainly, every form of authoritarianism degrades humanity. But the worst is that which hides behind a democratic facade, where the majority rules without regard for minorities.

Jinnah predicted this 80 years ago. While the military dictatorship he sought to avoid has plagued Pakistan, India's secular constitution has also been manipulated by every ruler for their own ends. Amendments are being made to India's secular laws, ensuring non-Hindus become reliant on the Hindu majority's mercy.

If the constitution guarantees equality under the law, freedom of expression, and other such rights, they remain merely words on paper. There's no hope for a better future unless we eliminate terms like 'majority' and 'minority' from our legal system and ensure equal rights for all citizens.

As long as our hypocrisy, sycophancy, and mediocrity prevail, long live Saadat Hasan Manto!
